sentence: Which summary stays within the survey's evidence?
setupText: Fifteen of the twenty people in your evening class say the new exercises help. No other classes were asked.
taskText: Which summary stays within the survey's evidence?
text: Fifteen of the twenty people in your evening class say the new exercises help. No other classes were asked. Which summary stays within the survey's evidence?
options: Most adults find the exercises helpful.
The exercises improve most adults' test scores.
The exercises are popular in several evening classes.
Most people in our class say the exercises help.
answer: Most people in our class say the exercises help.
explanation: 'Most' fits fifteen out of twenty; 'in our class' limits the group, and 'say' identifies opinions rather than measured improvement.

This extends the result from one class to adults generally.
rationales.Most people in our class say the exercis: 'Most' fits fifteen out of twenty; 'in our class' limits the group, and 'say' identifies opinions rather than measured improvement.
rationales.The exercises improve most adults' test: The survey asks about helpfulness; it does not measure test scores or represent most adults.
rationales.The exercises are popular in several eve: Only one class was asked, so several classes are outside the evidence.

sentence: Which message accurately reports her view?
setupText: A mechanic says the noise could come from a loose belt, but she needs to inspect the engine.
taskText: Which message accurately reports her view?
text: A mechanic says the noise could come from a loose belt, but she needs to inspect the engine. Which message accurately reports her view?
options: The mechanic found a loose belt.
The mechanic thinks the belt is unlikely to be loose.
A loose belt is one possible cause of the noise.
The noise means the belt needs replacing.
answer: A loose belt is one possible cause of the noise.
explanation: 'One possible cause' keeps the explanation tentative pending inspection.

She has not inspected the engine; 'found' turns a possible cause into a discovery.
rationales.The mechanic thinks the belt is unlikely: She offers a loose belt as a possibility, without calling it unlikely.
rationales.A loose belt is one possible cause of th: 'One possible cause' keeps the explanation tentative pending inspection.
rationales.The noise means the belt needs replacing: This assumes the cause and a particular repair, neither of which is confirmed.

sentence: Which answer explicitly preserves both the six-to-eight-hour range and its status as an estimate?
setupText: You are estimating the time needed to pack an office. You expect six to eight hours.
taskText: Which answer explicitly preserves both the six-to-eight-hour range and its status as an estimate?
text: You are estimating the time needed to pack an office. You expect six to eight hours. Which answer explicitly preserves both the six-to-eight-hour range and its status as an estimate?
options: It should take roughly a working day.
I expect it to take between six and eight hours.
It will take at least eight hours.
It will be finished in six hours.
answer: I expect it to take between six and eight hours.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b1-1603:Preserving a forecast range and its uncertainty
explanation: 'I expect' marks a forecast, and 'between six and eight' states both ends of the estimated range.

This is a reasonable rough approximation, but it does not explicitly retain the requested six-to-eight-hour range.
Eight was the upper end of your estimate, not the minimum.
This turns the shortest estimate into a firm completion time.
rationales.I expect it to take between six and eigh: 'I expect' marks a forecast, and 'between six and eight' states both ends of the estimated range.

sentence: Which reply does both?
setupText: You disagree with a colleague's plan because it leaves no time for testing. You want to raise this concern politely and clearly.
taskText: Which reply does both?
text: You disagree with a colleague's plan because it leaves no time for testing. You want to raise this concern politely and clearly. Which reply does both?
options: I'm not sure what the plan is.
The plan leaves enough time for testing.
I'm not sure the plan leaves enough time for testing.
Testing time is something we have already agreed on.
answer: I'm not sure the plan leaves enough time for testing.
explanation: 'I'm not sure' can soften disagreement. Naming the lack of testing time keeps the objection clear despite that polite wording.

rationales.I'm not sure the plan leaves enough time: 'I'm not sure' can soften disagreement. Naming the lack of testing time keeps the objection clear despite that polite wording.
This expresses lack of understanding, not your concern about testing time.
This agrees with the point you actually doubt.
rationales.Testing time is something we have alread: This presents agreement as settled instead of raising the concern.

sentence: Which sentence treats the menu as a possible cause without claiming it was the only change that mattered?
setupText: Bookings rose after a restaurant changed its menu. It also began offering cheaper lunches that week.
taskText: Which sentence treats the menu as a possible cause without claiming it was the only change that mattered?
text: Bookings rose after a restaurant changed its menu. It also began offering cheaper lunches that week. Which sentence treats the menu as a possible cause without claiming it was the only change that mattered?
options: The menu change may have helped increase bookings.
Bookings rose because the menu changed.
The menu change was less important than the cheaper lunches.
The new menu made the cheaper lunches more popular.
answer: The menu change may have helped increase bookings.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b1-1605:May have helped for a possible past contribution
explanation: 'May have helped' allows a contribution from the menu and leaves room for the cheaper lunches.

This states the menu as the cause without the requested uncertainty.
rationales.The menu change may have helped increase: 'May have helped' allows a contribution from the menu and leaves room for the cheaper lunches.
rationales.The menu change was less important than: The information does not compare the importance of the two changes.
rationales.The new menu made the cheaper lunches mo: This invents a link between the menu and lunch popularity.

sentence: Which statement describes a tendency while keeping the exceptions possible?
setupText: Your train has arrived late on seven of the last ten journeys, but not on every journey.
taskText: Which statement describes a tendency while keeping the exceptions possible?
text: Your train has arrived late on seven of the last ten journeys, but not on every journey. Which statement describes a tendency while keeping the exceptions possible?
options: This train tends to arrive late.
This train is due to arrive late.
This train used to arrive late.
This train is too late to catch.
answer: This train tends to arrive late.
explanation: 'Tends to' describes a repeated pattern without saying it happens on every journey.

'Tends to' describes a repeated pattern without saying it happens on every journey.
'Is due to' concerns an expected arrival, not the repeated pattern across journeys.
'Used to' presents a past habit, often suggesting it has changed; that is not stated here.
This describes a particular timing problem rather than how often the train is late.

sentence: What does this wording tell you?
setupText: A hotel advertises rooms 'from $90 a night'. You have not selected a room or a date.
taskText: What does this wording tell you?
text: A hotel advertises rooms 'from $90 a night'. You have not selected a room or a date. What does this wording tell you?
options: Your room will cost no more than $90.
The usual room price is around $90.
The hotel has reduced each room by $90.
The advertised starting price is $90.
answer: The advertised starting price is $90.
explanation: 'From $90' identifies the lowest advertised price; your selected stay may cost more.

'From' gives a starting price, not a maximum for your room.
A starting price does not establish the usual price.
'From $90' identifies the lowest advertised price; your selected stay may cost more.
'From $90' states a price, not a discount amount.

sentence: Which paraphrase preserves the difference between a target and a promise?
setupText: An email says, 'We aim to reply within two working days.'
taskText: Which paraphrase preserves the difference between a target and a promise?
text: An email says, 'We aim to reply within two working days.' Which paraphrase preserves the difference between a target and a promise?
options: Replies are promised within two working days.
Replies normally arrive after two working days.
Replies take exactly two working days.
The goal is to reply within two working days.
answer: The goal is to reply within two working days.
explanation: 'The goal is' keeps the intended target without presenting it as a guarantee.

rationales.Replies are promised within two working: 'Aim to' sets a target; 'promised' makes a stronger commitment.
rationales.Replies normally arrive after two workin: The target is within two days, and the email gives no actual reply pattern.
'Within' allows earlier replies and 'aim' does not promise an exact duration.
rationales.The goal is to reply within two working: 'The goal is' keeps the intended target without presenting it as a guarantee.

sentence: Which wording is accurate for that purpose?
setupText: Your notes say the repair cost was $247. You are writing a casual message and want to round to the nearest $50.
taskText: Which wording is accurate for that purpose?
text: Your notes say the repair cost was $247. You are writing a casual message and want to round to the nearest $50. Which wording is accurate for that purpose?
options: The repair cost just over $250.
The repair cost a minimum of $250.
The repair cost approximately $250.
The repair cost exactly $250.
answer: The repair cost approximately $250.
explanation: $250 is the nearest multiple of $50; 'approximately' signals the rounding.

$247 is below $250, so 'over' gives the wrong direction.
$250 is the nearest multiple of $50; 'approximately' signals the rounding.
The actual cost is less than the claimed minimum.
Rounding $247 does not make $250 the exact amount paid.

sentence: Which sentence answers without unnecessary uncertainty?
setupText: A team checked every entry on an attendance sheet and found 36 names. The report asks for the checked count.
taskText: Which sentence answers without unnecessary uncertainty?
text: A team checked every entry on an attendance sheet and found 36 names. The report asks for the checked count. Which sentence answers without unnecessary uncertainty?
options: There appear to be several dozen names.
There may be 36 names on the sheet.
The sheet contains 36 names.
The sheet should contain about 36 names.
answer: The sheet contains 36 names.
explanation: 'Contains 36 names' states a checked count directly. May, about, or should would wrongly turn that result into a possibility, estimate, or expectation.

This replaces a checked count with an uncertain, vague description.
'May be' casts doubt on a number the team has checked.
'Contains 36 names' states a checked count directly. May, about, or should would wrongly turn that result into a possibility, estimate, or expectation.
'Should' describes an expectation and 'about' an estimate, not the completed count.

sentence: Which conclusion is supported?
setupText: A note says, 'Not all visitors need a parking permit.' It does not say how many do.
taskText: Which conclusion is supported?
text: A note says, 'Not all visitors need a parking permit.' It does not say how many do. Which conclusion is supported?
options: Most visitors do not need a permit.
No visitors need a permit.
Exactly half the visitors need a permit.
Some visitors do not need a permit.
answer: Some visitors do not need a permit.
explanation: 'Not all' means there are exceptions to the requirement; it does not give their number.

'Not all' means there are exceptions to the requirement; it does not give their number.
The note does not say whether the exceptions form a majority.
This removes the requirement for everyone, which 'not all' does not establish.
The note contains no number or proportion.

sentence: Which reply keeps the limit of your knowledge clear?
setupText: You read a timetable online last month. You believe the last bus leaves at eleven, but it may have changed.
taskText: Which reply keeps the limit of your knowledge clear?
text: You read a timetable online last month. You believe the last bus leaves at eleven, but it may have changed. Which reply keeps the limit of your knowledge clear?
options: As far as I know, the last bus leaves at eleven.
The last bus has been changed to eleven.
The current timetable confirms an eleven o'clock bus.
I doubt there is a bus at eleven.
answer: As far as I know, the last bus leaves at eleven.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b1-1612:As far as I know for limited knowledge
explanation: 'As far as I know' limits the claim to your possibly outdated information.

This asserts a change that you have not checked.
rationales.The current timetable confirms an eleven: You have not seen the current timetable.
This expresses doubt about the bus, whereas you believe it runs then.
rationales.As far as I know, the last bus leaves at: 'As far as I know' limits the claim to your possibly outdated information.

sentence: Which message fits?
setupText: The manager says, 'We expect the repairs to finish on Thursday.' You need to report the expected day without making it a confirmed date.
taskText: Which message fits?
text: The manager says, 'We expect the repairs to finish on Thursday.' You need to report the expected day without making it a confirmed date. Which message fits?
options: The repairs are expected to finish on Thursday.
Thursday has been confirmed as the finishing date.
Thursday is the latest possible finishing date.
The repairs must finish before Thursday.
answer: The repairs are expected to finish on Thursday.
explanation: 'Are expected to' preserves the forecast and the stated day.

rationales.The repairs are expected to finish on Th: 'Are expected to' preserves the forecast and the stated day.
rationales.Thursday is the latest possible finishin: An expected date is not necessarily the latest possible date.
This changes the forecast into a requirement and moves the deadline earlier.

sentence: Which paraphrase preserves the contrast between narrowness and possible wheelchair access?
setupText: A report says, 'The new entrance is fairly narrow, but wheelchair users can pass through.'
taskText: Which paraphrase preserves the contrast between narrowness and possible wheelchair access?
text: A report says, 'The new entrance is fairly narrow, but wheelchair users can pass through.' Which paraphrase preserves the contrast between narrowness and possible wheelchair access?
options: The entrance is narrow enough to prevent wheelchair access.
The entrance is narrow, but it still allows wheelchair access.
The entrance is wider than wheelchair users need.
The entrance is only for wheelchair users.
answer: The entrance is narrow, but it still allows wheelchair access.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b1-1614:Separating a limiting description from an access restriction
explanation: 'But' contrasts the limited width with access that remains possible. Narrow does not mean too narrow to pass through.

rationales.The entrance is narrow enough to prevent: This reverses the statement that wheelchair users can pass through.
rationales.The entrance is wider than wheelchair us: The report does not compare the width with the space users need.
rationales.The entrance is narrow, but it still all: 'But' contrasts the limited width with access that remains possible. Narrow does not mean too narrow to pass through.
rationales.The entrance is only for wheelchair user: The report describes access, not a restriction on who may use the entrance.

sentence: Which opening keeps that personal limit?
setupText: You are writing about your own use of a budgeting app. It helped you notice small purchases; you do not know how it worked for other users.
taskText: Which opening keeps that personal limit?
text: You are writing about your own use of a budgeting app. It helped you notice small purchases; you do not know how it worked for other users. Which opening keeps that personal limit?
options: For most users, the app makes small purchases easier to notice.
In my experience, the app made small purchases easier to notice.
The app is designed to prevent small purchases.
Other users probably noticed fewer small purchases.
answer: In my experience, the app made small purchases easier to notice.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b1-1615:In my experience as an evidence boundary
explanation: 'In my experience' limits the benefit to what happened when you used the app.

rationales.In my experience, the app made small pur: 'In my experience' limits the benefit to what happened when you used the app.
rationales.For most users, the app makes small purc: You have no information about most users.
rationales.The app is designed to prevent small pur: Noticing purchases does not establish that preventing them is the app's purpose.
rationales.Other users probably noticed fewer small: This guesses about other users and changes the reported effect.

sentence: Which sentence preserves both the number limit and the uncertainty?
setupText: A service announcement says, 'Some deliveries may be delayed.'
taskText: Which sentence preserves both the number limit and the uncertainty?
text: A service announcement says, 'Some deliveries may be delayed.' Which sentence preserves both the number limit and the uncertainty?
options: Some deliveries have been delayed.
There is a possibility of delays to some deliveries.
Most deliveries are likely to be delayed.
Deliveries will be delayed by a few days.
answer: There is a possibility of delays to some deliveries.
explanation: 'Some' leaves the number unspecified, while 'a possibility' expresses the same uncertainty as may. Neither word establishes that a delay has occurred.

This changes a possible delay into a reported event.
rationales.Most deliveries are likely to be delayed: This changes both 'some' to 'most' and possibility to likelihood.
rationales.Deliveries will be delayed by a few days: This adds certainty and a duration that the announcement does not give.
rationales.There is a possibility of delays to some: 'Some' leaves the number unspecified, while 'a possibility' expresses the same uncertainty as may. Neither word establishes that a delay has occurred.

sentence: Which reply accepts it as worth trying without claiming it will meet your needs?

taskText: Which reply accepts it as worth trying without claiming it will meet your needs?
text: You need a quiet room. A colleague offers Room B, but you have never worked there. Which reply accepts it as worth trying without claiming it will meet your needs?

answer: Room B could work; let's try it.

This claims knowledge of the room's conditions that you do not have.
'Could work' treats success as possible, and 'let's try it' accepts a trial.
rationales.Room B probably won't work; let's find a: This rejects the trial and predicts failure, contrary to the requested reply.
You have never worked there, so this invents experience.

sentence: Which reply keeps your price judgment within what you checked?
setupText: Your friend asks whether a restaurant is expensive. You have seen the lunch menu, but not the dinner menu.

answer: The lunch prices look reasonable to me.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b1-1618:Limiting a price judgment to inspected information
explanation: 'Lunch prices' names the information inspected; 'look reasonable to me' marks a personal price judgment, not a conclusion about the unseen dinner menu.

You have not seen the dinner prices, so even 'seems' lacks the stated basis.
rationales.It is cheaper than the other restaurants: You have no prices for the other restaurants.
'Lunch prices' names the information inspected; 'look reasonable to me' marks a personal price judgment, not a conclusion about the unseen dinner menu.
rationales.The restaurant recently lowered its pric: One menu does not establish a recent price change.

'Slightly' describes the small difference stated by the technician.

sentence: Which interpretation fits?

'Mainly' names the principal audience, and the second clause permits experienced staff.
rationales.Beginners and experienced staff are equa: 'Mainly for beginners' gives beginners a more central place.
rationales.Experienced staff must attend the worksh: 'May attend' allows attendance; it does not require it.
